title: NumPy Examples
description: Small NumPy examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: Make a number array
examples.description: A NumPy array holds values with a shared data type. np.array builds one from a Python list.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

scores = np.array([2, 4, 6])
print(scores.tolist())

examples.title: Read the shape
examples.description: Shape tells you the size of each dimension. A table-like array has a row count and a column count.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

grid = np.array([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])
print(grid.shape)

examples.title: Choose a data type
examples.description: A data type describes how values are stored. An explicit type avoids guessing when size or precision matters.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

values = np.array([1, 2], dtype=np.float32)
print(values.dtype)

examples.title: Index a position
examples.description: An index selects a position. NumPy, like Python lists, starts counting at zero.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

values = np.array([5, 7, 9])
print(values[1])

examples.title: Slice a range
examples.description: A slice selects a range. Its starting index is included and its stopping index is excluded.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

values = np.array([2, 4, 6, 8])
print(values[1:3].tolist())

examples.title: Calculate element by element
examples.description: Adding two arrays of the same shape adds matching positions. This is element-wise addition.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

a = np.array([1, 2, 3])
b = np.array([10, 20, 30])
print((a + b).tolist())

examples.title: Broadcast one value
examples.description: Broadcasting lets some differently shaped values work together. A single number can be used for every item in an array.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

scores = np.array([2, 4, 6])
print((scores + 1).tolist())

examples.title: Sum along an axis
examples.description: An axis is one direction through an array. For this two-dimensional table, axis 0 combines rows to produce a total for each column.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

grid = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
print(grid.sum(axis=0).tolist())

examples.title: Reshape without changing the count
examples.description: reshape changes the arrangement of values. The new shape must hold the same total number of values.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

values = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6])
print(values.reshape(2, 3).tolist())

examples.title: Filter with a boolean mask
examples.description: A boolean mask is a list of true-or-false choices. True positions are kept when used to select array values.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

scores = np.array([3, 8, 5])
mask = scores >= 5
print(scores[mask].tolist())

examples.title: Make an independent copy
examples.description: A copy owns separate data. It is useful when changing a result must not change the original array.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

original = np.array([1, 2, 3])
copy = original.copy()
copy[0] = 99
print(original.tolist())

examples.title: Summarise a small dataset
examples.description: The mean is the total divided by the number of values. The minimum and maximum describe the range.
examples.code:
import numpy as np

scores = np.array([2, 4, 6])
print(float(scores.mean()), int(scores.min()), int(scores.max()))
